title: Present Subjunctive: Introduction
summary: Use the present subjunctive after wishes, doubts, emotions, and impersonal expressions.

sections.heading: Why the subjunctive exists
sections.body: The **subjunctive** presents an action as desired, uncertain, emotional, necessary, or not yet real. It often appears in a dependent clause introduced by **que**.

examples.en: I doubt he will come today.

examples.pt: É importante que a gente chegue cedo.
examples.en: It is important that we arrive early.

sections.heading: Regular formation
sections.body:
For regular verbs, start from the **eu** form of the present, remove **-o**, and add the opposite vowel endings: -ar verbs use **e**, -er/-ir verbs use **a**.

| Infinitive | Present subjunctive examples |
|---|---|
| falar | que eu fale, que eles falem |
| comer | que eu coma, que eles comam |
| abrir | que eu abra, que eles abram |

examples.en: I want her to talk to me.

examples.pt: Prefiro que você abra a janela.
examples.en: I prefer that you open the window.

sections.heading: Common irregulars
sections.body: Very common verbs have irregular subjunctive forms: **ser → seja**, **estar → esteja**, **ter → tenha**, **ir → vá**, **saber → saiba**, **fazer → faça**, **poder → possa**.

keyPoints: Subjunctive often follows que after desire, doubt, emotion, and necessity.
Regular -ar verbs use e endings; -er/-ir verbs use a endings.
Talvez often triggers the subjunctive when uncertainty is real.
Learn common irregulars early: seja, esteja, tenha, vá, faça, possa.

commonMistakes.wrong: É importante que nós chegamos cedo.
commonMistakes.right: É importante que nós cheguemos cedo.
commonMistakes.note: Necessity uses subjunctive; chegar has spelling change.
